target_subject: convex safety mirror mounted on a pole

scene: A convex mirror reflects a green train stopped at a station platform against a partly cloudy sky.
The mirror is affixed to a black pole attached to a pale yellow wall with red graffiti on the lower left.
Overhead catenary wires and leafy tree branches appear in the mirror's reflection above the train.
action: The train is stationary at the platform, with visible passengers inside one window.
The mirror captures a distorted wide-angle view of the scene behind the observer.
Red spray-painted graffiti marks the wall beneath the mirror but does not interact with it.
rationale: The train’s alignment with the platform edge and lack of motion blur suggest it is stopped, though no brake lights or door status are visible.
The curvature of the mirror causes radial distortion, confirming it is convex; this is standard for traffic/safety mirrors.
The presence of overhead wires and train design indicate an electrified rail system, but the specific country or operator cannot be determined from visible evidence.
object: A circular convex mirror with a black metal rim is mounted vertically on a black cylindrical pole.
The reflected image shows a green train with yellow horizontal stripes and multiple rectangular windows, including one showing a seated passenger.
The platform edge is marked by a white tactile paving strip adjacent to the train’s doors.
A pale yellow concrete wall forms the background, bearing red graffiti reading 'MOK' in stylized capital letters.
Above the mirror, bare and leafy branches of trees extend into the sky, partially reflected in the mirror’s upper portion.

symbolic_mapping: the mirror’s curvature maps to mediated perception
the train’s stillness maps to suspended temporality
philosophy_interpretations.interpretation: The convex mirror presents reality as inherently distorted and partial, suggesting that knowledge is always mediated and never direct; the train paused at the platform evokes a moment arrested in time, highlighting mortality’s constraint on movement and continuity.
alternative_interpretations: It is simply a functional safety device capturing a routine transit scene without symbolic intent.
limitations: No textual or contextual cues confirm intentional symbolism; distortion may be purely optical, not epistemological.

symbolic_mapping: graffiti as unauthorized mark contrasts with institutional infrastructure
color juxtaposition signals tension between individual expression and system uniformity
philosophy_interpretations.interpretation: The graffiti asserts an individual trace against the standardized backdrop of public transit infrastructure, embodying the persistent negotiation between personal agency and systemic constraint within shared social space.
alternative_interpretations: The graffiti is incidental vandalism with no intended commentary on social structure.
limitations: The graffiti’s content ('MOK') is ambiguous and lacks legible message; its authorship and intent are unseen.

symbolic_mapping: single visible person represents anonymity within collective transit
mirror frames only part of the scene, implying exclusion of context
philosophy_interpretations.interpretation: The lone visible passenger appears only as a silhouette within a constrained frame, illustrating how identity is reduced to appearance under surveillance-like observation, while the mirror’s boundary enforces relational incompleteness—what is seen is necessarily disconnected from the whole.
alternative_interpretations: The passenger is merely coincidentally positioned where the mirror captures them; no thematic emphasis is intended.
limitations: Only one person is clearly discernible; others may be present but obscured by reflections or angle.
